caption: A rescuer in a red helmet and hi-vis clothing helps an elderly woman climb over rubble and down steps from a damaged building.

West Yorkshire, UK Andy Burnham views an illegal rubbish dump beside Bradford City’s Valley Parade stadium. The prime minister has announced a new crackdown on illegal waste dumping and action to clear up communities.

Osaka, Japan Attenders take pictures of Johannes Vermeer’s famous painting during the press preview for Vermeer’s Girl with a Pearl Earring: Dutch masterpieces of the 17th century, an exhibition at the Nakanoshima Museum of Art.
St Pölten, Austria Cooling down in the river Traisen on the sidelines of the Frequency 2026 music festival.

Glasgow, UK Members of the Unite, Unison and GMB unions protest outside Glasgow City Chambers to coincide with a vote on a new pay and grading scheme for council employees. The unions claim the proposals would adversely affect low-paid workers, particularly women, who they say have been underpaid for two decades.
Lancashire, UK The education secretary, Lucy Powell, speaks with students collecting their GCSE results at Harper Green school in Farnworth, Bolton.

Yeoncheon, South Korea US soldiers set up a floating bridge on a river at a military training field during joint US-South Korean exercises. Donald Trump has announced a decision to scale back the joint drills. Kim Yo-jong, the influential sister of the North Korean leader, Kim Jong-un, has dismissed the importance of this, saying it was not worthy of comment.
Hautvillers, France Chardonnay grapes are harvested at the Gobillard vineyard in the Champagne region.

Ceuta, Spain People who were sleeping rough on El Trampolín beach are transferred to a shelter. The Spanish government is providing temporary shelter for 1,800 migrants who were staying on the beach and in the Loma Colmenar area of Ceuta, and plans to gradually expand these facilities.

Kyiv, Ukraine A rescuer helps a woman at the site of a Russian missile strike on a residential area. At least 14 people died and more than 40 others were injured in an overnight Russian attack by drones and missiles of different types on Kyiv and the region, according to the Ukrainian State Emergency Service (SES).

Khan Younis, Gaza A woman swims during an activity organised for young Palestinians who have lost limbs. Basic swimming training and aquatic exercise programmes under the supervision of professional coaches support physical development and ease psychological trauma.

Ankara, Turkey Vibrant hues are caused on Lake Tuz by increased salinity, high temperatures, and microalgae producing beta-carotene. On the Unesco World Heritage Tentative List for its unique ecological features, rich biodiversity and avian significance, the hyper-saline lake attracts tourists who come to witness the striking natural colour transformation in summer.

Shenzhen, China Hui Ka Yan, 67, the founder of Evergrande Group, one of China’s largest property developers, stands at the Intermediate People’s Court in Guangdong province, where he was sentenced to life in prison after pleading guilty to charges of fraud.
Banda Aceh, Indonesia People watch as a woman is caned after being convicted of violating Islamic law prohibiting sex outside marriage.

Apalit, Philippines A residential area is seriously flooded due to monsoon rains in Pampanga. The lingering monsoon effects, compounded with the intensifying tropical storm Saudel that is expected to turn into a typhoon, have brought heavy rains causing widespread and serious flooding across 10 different regions of the Philippines, including Central Luzon. Tens of thousands of people have been displaced or evacuated to safety.
Washington DC, US Donald Trump speaks before signing a piece of stone at the construction site of a helipad on the South Lawn of the White House.
A woman dressed as Cruella de Vil with her robot dalmatians in Beijing, China.
Khan Younis, Gaza Strip A makeshift swimming pool lined with aid tarpaulins in a displacement camp.
Paposo, Chile Bulldozers work to reopen a mountain road damaged by flooding and landslides.
Gaza City, Gaza Strip People grieve over the bodies of relatives killed in an Israeli drone strike on a beachfront cafe.
Pereira, Colombia Rescuers retrieve an earthquake victim from the rubble.
Rawalpindi, Pakistan A resident bails floodwater out of his home after heavy rains.
Seoul, South Korea Soldiers take part in an anti-terror drill at a hotel.
Ayetoro, Nigeria A man walks past abandoned buildings damaged by coastal erosion.
Deliblatska Peščara, Serbia Firefighters battle a wildfire.
Florida, US A Japanese sea nettle at the town’s Jellyfish Museum in Pompano Beach.
Melbourne, Australia A stablehand washes down a racehorse.
Dearborn, US A neo-Nazi protester takes part in a far-right rally outside the Henry Ford Centennial Library in the Michigan city.
Tehran, Iran An anti-US billboard at a busy junction.
Baelen, Belgium A firefighter involved in tackling a wildfire at the Hautes Fagnes nature reserve.
Conwy, Wales An artwork by Greenpeace addresses the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham.
El Alto, Bolivia A woman boards a bus during a snow shower.
Aerial view of sheep penned in fenced enclosures at the Lairg sheep auction, Scotland.

Lusaka, Zambia Supporters of president-elect, Hakainde Hichilema, celebrate his reelection for a second term. The 64-year-old, credited with restructuring the country’s debt and making schooling free, won with around 60% of the vote.

Jakarta, Indonesia University students jostle with police officers during a protest against government policies, including state budget spending, the free meals programme and expanded military roles in civilian affairs.
Cambridge, England Floral tributes to the late Cambridge professor Jason Arday are left outside Senate House after his death at age 41.
Waimes, Belgium Firefighters attend a wildfire in Waimes, in the Hautes Fagnes region.

Moscow, Russia Japan’s ambassador to Russia, Akira Muto, leaves the Russian foreign ministry after a tit-for-tat summoning by Tokyo and Moscow, sparked by Putin’s visit to Iturup, a disputed island known in Japan as Etorofu.

Kyiv, Ukraine An honour guard holds a portrait of Col Yevhen Konovalets beside his grave during a reburial ceremony at the national military memorial cemetery. Konovalets, a military commander and leader of the Ukrainian nationalist movement, was assassinated in Rotterdam in 1938. His remains have been repatriated from the Netherlands after 88 years.

Washington DC, US The renovated Arts of War statues, newly covered in gold leaf, at Arlington Memorial Bridge near the Lincoln Memorial. The Trump administration has ordered a $5.1m restoration project to regild the two Arts of War statues, along with the nearby Arts of Peace companion statues. The four statues are being restored under a project overseen by the US Department of the Interior.
Auckland, New Zealand A look card backstage ahead of the twenty-seven names show at New Zealand fashion week.
London, England Artist Clare Twomey at the press preview of the War Child x Secret 7” exhibition at 180 Studios, where 700 sleeves will be auctioned to raise money for children affected by war.
Shanghai, China Tourists visit a giant 13-metre-long dachshund installation at the Haus Nowhere store on Huaihai Middle Road.
